sections.h2: What should you know before selling a house in Brookhaven, NY?
sections.html:
Brookhaven is a very large Suffolk County town on Long Island, so a sale here depends first on which hamlet or village the house is in, then on three offices: the Town Assessor, the Town Building Division and the Suffolk County Clerk. The Census Bureau estimates 496,410 residents for July 1, 2025, up from 485,773 counted in 2020.

For 2020 to 2024 the Census lists a median owner-occupied home value of $489,200, an owner-occupied rate of 80.9% and 166,521 households averaging 2.85 people. Median owner costs are $3,101 a month with a mortgage and $1,377 without one, and median gross rent is $2,314.

The rest of this page explains how the town is laid out, how assessments and exemptions work, what the Building Division handles, and how a deed is recorded in Suffolk County.

sections.h2: Where is Brookhaven and which communities does it include?
sections.html:
The town reaches from Long Island Sound on the north to the Atlantic on the south and takes in part of Fire Island. It covers 259.65 square miles of land, about 1,870 people per square mile, and its first English settlement, Setauket, was established in 1655. The town includes eight incorporated villages and roughly 50 hamlets.

  • Port Jefferson and Stony Brook: Port Jefferson is a downtown and the ferry terminal for Bridgeport, Connecticut, and Stony Brook is home to the university. Setauket, where the town began, sits between them.
  • Patchogue, Bellport and Mastic-Shirley: South Shore communities on the Great South Bay side, served by the Montauk Branch of the railroad.
  • Farmingville, Medford and Yaphank: inland hamlets. Bald Hill in Farmingville marks the point where the glacier that formed Long Island stopped.

Two research institutions anchor the economy. Stony Brook University is the town's largest employer, and Brookhaven National Laboratory in Upton and the university together account for about half of the employees at the town's ten biggest employers. Tourism is also a major part of the local economy.

sections.h2: How does commuting shape Brookhaven house prices?
sections.html:
Mean travel time to work is 32.3 minutes, and the Long Island Rail Road is a large part of why people live near a station. Three LIRR lines cross the town: the Main Line, with stops at Medford and Yaphank and Ronkonkoma station on the Islip-Brookhaven town line; the Montauk Branch, with Patchogue, Bellport and Mastic-Shirley; and the Port Jefferson Branch, with Stony Brook and Port Jefferson.

Suffolk County Transit provides bus service, and the Village of Patchogue runs its own local buses. A listing near a station should state the distance, since commuters ask.

Median household income is $120,110 and per capita income is $50,807. About 91.7% of residents kept the same address over the past year, so the typical owner has been in place a long time and often holds large equity.

sections.h2: How do assessments and exemptions work in Brookhaven?
sections.html:
The Town Assessor's Office values more than 184,000 parcels for taxation, keeps ownership current from recorded deeds and tracks new construction, demolition and consolidation of lots. Its roll for 2026 to 2027 is posted, along with an interactive assessment roll where you can look up property and home valuations.

The office also approves real property tax exemptions for senior citizens, people with disabilities and veterans. Applications and renewals must be filed by March 1 each year, and the deadline for 2026 was March 2, 2026. That date has passed, so any exemption you want for the next tax year has to be filed by the following March. If you are selling before then, tell the buyer's attorney which exemptions currently reduce your bill.

Two online services help at sale time: a Certificate of Assessment application and a radius map and list application. The Assessor's Office is at One Independence Hill in Farmingville.

sections.h2: What does the Brookhaven Building Division handle?
sections.html:
The Building Division, part of the town's Planning Department, has moved to a Digital Services portal, and its paper drop-off has ended. Applications filed before September 28, 2026 can be traced through an online help form if you cannot find them in the new system.

  • Commercial applications, and residential ones filed by expeditors or licensed professionals, go through the portal.
  • Property owners can still file their own residential applications in person on paper, as long as every plan and supporting document is 8.5 by 11 inches.
  • The Division processes accessory apartment licenses, building construction permits, certificates of existing use, chain of title requests, house rental licenses, letters of correction and the voiding of permits or licenses.

If your house has an extra unit, a finished basement or a rental license, ask the Division which of those applications applies and whether anything is open. Tell any buyer, cash buyer included, about a rental license, since the buyer will want to know.

sections.h2: How do you record a deed in Suffolk County?
sections.html:
Deeds for Brookhaven property are recorded with the Suffolk County Clerk, whose recording unit examines each document and collects fees, mortgage tax and real estate transfer tax. The clerk will not fill out forms for you or correct a defect, so a mistake means rejection.

What a Brookhaven deed package needs at the Suffolk County Clerk
ItemRequirement
DeedNames and street addresses of all parties (no P.O. boxes), notarized seller signature, full property description
Cover sheetSuffolk County Recording and Endorsement page, legal size
RP-5217Real Property Transfer Report, filled in online and printed on legal paper
TP-584Transfer tax return, with Social Security or federal ID numbers for all parties
IT-2663Estimated income tax form for nonresident sellers

Source: Suffolk County Clerk, How to Record a Deed. Transfer tax applies when the price tops $500, at $2 per $500 or fraction thereof, and a 1% additional tax applies to residences at $1 million or more. The extra Peconic Bay form is only for the five East End towns, which do not include Brookhaven. Checks go to the Suffolk County Clerk, and the transfer tax needs a certified check, cash, money order or an approved attorney or title company check.

sections.h2: What selling routes are open to a Brookhaven owner?
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, try to sell yourself, or accept a cash offer. With a median value near $489,200, many Brookhaven owners have enough equity to cover repairs, but time is the cost: showings, inspections and a buyer's mortgage approval.

A cash offer fits houses with old systems in Farmingville or Medford, inherited homes on the South Shore, or a property with an unlicensed rental or apartment. Before you decide, compare the offer with what a listing would net after repairs, agent costs and carrying costs, and check your exemption status and rental license so the sale price is not the only number on the table.

faqs.q: Where do I get a copy of my Brookhaven assessment?
faqs.a: Use the Town Assessor's interactive assessment roll, or the 2026 to 2027 final roll posted on the town website. The office also runs an online Certificate of Assessment application. Visit One Independence Hill in Farmingville if you prefer an in-person answer.

faqs.q: Can I still file for a senior, disability or veteran exemption in Brookhaven?
faqs.a: Not for 2026. Filings were due by March 2, 2026, and the town's rule is that applications and renewals reach the Assessor by March 1 each year. File for the next cycle before the March deadline.

faqs.q: Do I need a house rental license to sell a rental in Brookhaven?
faqs.a: Ask the Building Division. It issues house rental licenses and accessory apartment licenses, and a buyer will want to know whether yours is in force. Settle the license status before you list so the closing does not stall.

faqs.q: Which county office records a Brookhaven deed?
faqs.a: The Suffolk County Clerk. The deed must carry names and street addresses of all parties, a notary acknowledgment, the RP-5217 and TP-584 forms, and original signatures. The clerk examines each package and cannot fix errors for you.

faqs.q: How much extra tax applies to a Brookhaven sale at $1 million or more?
faqs.a: A 1% mansion tax on the full price, paid by the buyer. Below $1 million the only transfer tax is the base rate of $2 per $500, which the seller pays. A $1,000,000 sale would add $10,000 for the buyer.
